title: Dynamical degrees of twisted rational maps
summary: Twisted rational maps arise naturally in relative algebraic dynamics: if a rational self-map preserves a fibration, then the induced map on the generic fiber is usually not an ordinary rational self-map over the function field, but a twisted one. This suggests that twisted rational maps form a natural framework for studying relative dynamics. In this framework we extend the theory of dynamical degrees, the numerical invariants measuring the asymptotic complexity of a dynamical system: the defining limits exist, are independent of the choice of polarization, and are birational invariants.
